questions.title: Two wires joined by a sliding lead
questions.summary: Same circuit idea as NYJC Q3: 1/I = Px + Q. Measure d_F, plot 1/I against x, then use P/Q = (d_G²/d_F² − 1)/L to work out d_G.

xlsx.desc: Seven (x, I) pairs. Plot 1/I against x, find P and Q, then d_G.

questions.title: Two stretched rubber bands
questions.summary: A mass hangs from two rubber bands on a hacksaw blade. Keeping the band length b fixed keeps the tension fixed, so sin α = Cm with C = g/(2ek). Then analyse a non-Hookean force–extension dataset: work done from area, hysteresis, and B from ln(F/A + 1) against x.

xlsx.desc: A practice version of the engineer's loading data. Area under F–x (trapezium) for the work done; plot ln(F/A + 1) against x for B.

questions.title: Coupled pendulums
questions.summary: Two pendulums hang from a common string. Energy passes from A to B and back; time how long A takes to stop and see how it depends on separation, tension, length difference and mass, then plan a test of independence from release angle.

xlsx.desc: Sample t against x readings plus Table 3.2. Plot t against (m₂ − m₁) and extrapolate to equal masses.

2.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 612.00 792.00" font-family="DejaVu Sans, Verdana, Geneva, sans-serif"><g class="ans" data-q="Q1"><text x="130.0" y="179.0" font-size="9" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">zero error = 0.00 mm; readings at three points: 0.27, 0.28, 0.27 mm</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q1"><text x="400.7" y="213.4" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">0.27 mm</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q1"><text x="400.1" y="599.8" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">50.0 cm</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q1"><text x="398.8" y="631.6" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">0.258 A</text></g></svg>

notes.text: Two marks for the micrometer: a sensible value (≈ 0.2–0.5 mm) to 0.01 mm, and evidence of repeats or a zero-error check.
Position C at exactly 50.0 cm on both rules. Read the clip edge against the scale at eye level.
Seven values from 10 cm to 90 cm, with 1/I calculated in the table: that is the evidence for the [3].
Units: P in A⁻¹ m⁻¹ (x in m) and Q in A⁻¹.

4.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 612.00 792.00" font-family="DejaVu Sans, Verdana, Geneva, sans-serif"><g class="ans" data-q="Q1"><text x="130.0" y="239.8" font-size="9.8" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">d_G² / d_F² = 1 + LP/Q = 1 + 1.000 × 3.496/2.126 = 2.644</text><text x="130.0" y="252.5" font-size="9.8" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">d_G = 0.27 × √2.644</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q1"><text x="400.7" y="318.9" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">0.44 mm</text></g></svg>

notes.text: Show the rearrangement before substituting values. Give d_G to the same precision as d_F.

5.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 612.00 792.00" font-family="DejaVu Sans, Verdana, Geneva, sans-serif"><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="416.1" y="550.1" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">300 g</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="140.0" y="733.6" font-size="8.6" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">Protractor centred where the band leaves the blade; rule laid along the band</text><text x="140.0" y="744.8" font-size="8.6" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">from the blade to the hook.</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="409.9" y="656.4" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">65°</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="410.9" y="686.8" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">9.4 cm</text></g></svg>

notes.text: α is between ONE band and the blade. Read it at the top where the band leaves the blade.
Measure b along the band (top of band on the blade to the hook), to 0.1 cm.

6.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 612.00 792.00" font-family="DejaVu Sans, Verdana, Geneva, sans-serif"><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="410.0" y="183.0" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">200 g</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="406.9" y="243.9" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">37°</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="140.0" y="359.6" font-size="9.6" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">C = sin α / m</text><text x="140.0" y="372.1" font-size="9.6" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">C₁ = sin 65° / 0.300 = 3.021</text><text x="140.0" y="384.6" font-size="9.6" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">C₂ = sin 37° / 0.200 = 3.009</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="408.1" y="426.1" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">3.02 kg⁻¹</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="406.5" y="456.6" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">3.01 kg⁻¹</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="140.0" y="609.3" font-size="9.3" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">unstretched length of one band l₀ = 6.0 cm ⇒ e = b − l₀ = 3.4 cm</text><text x="140.0" y="621.4" font-size="9.3" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">k = g/(2eC) = 9.81 / (2 × 0.034 × 3.02)  (mean C)</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="408.2" y="695.5" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">48 N m⁻¹</text></g></svg>

notes.text: Keeping b the same keeps the extension, and so the tension T, the same. Then 2T sin α = mg gives sin α ∝ m.
Write C with its unit (kg⁻¹ if m is in kg) to 2–3 s.f.
You need an extra measurement: the unstretched length of a band, to find e. Show it in your working.

7.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 612.00 792.00" font-family="DejaVu Sans, Verdana, Geneva, sans-serif"><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="100.3" y="105.4" font-size="9.2" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">The bands are not straight lines of zero width: they flatten and twist at the blade and the</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="100.3" y="130.7" font-size="9.2" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">hook, so it is hard to decide where to place the protractor to measure α (and where b</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="100.3" y="156.0" font-size="9.2" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">starts and ends).</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="384.2" y="380.2" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">0.218 </text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="128.7" y="436.7" font-size="9.2" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">Work done = area under the force–extension graph, found with the trapezium rule</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q2"><text x="128.7" y="461.9" font-size="9.2" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">in the spreadsheet: Σ ½(Fₙ + Fₙ₊₁)Δx.</text></g></svg>

notes.text: Make the error specific to this set-up (band shape at blade/hook, or b changing while you adjust the tops).
Non-Hookean means the graph is a curve. The area under it is still the work done; 0.5 × F × x does not apply.
One mark: the loop area = energy lost as heat per cycle.
Linearise: ln(F/A + 1) = Bx, a straight line through the origin with gradient B.

10.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 612.00 792.00" font-family="DejaVu Sans, Verdana, Geneva, sans-serif"><g class="ans" data-q="Q3"><text x="404.9" y="193.2" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">15.0</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q3"><text x="180.0" y="339.0" font-size="9" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">Times from release to A first stopping: 20.1 s, 21.6 s, 20.7 s → mean</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q3"><text x="403.6" y="382.4" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">20.8</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q3"><text x="180.0" y="439.0" font-size="9" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">Δt ≈ (21.6 − 20.1)/2 ≈ 0.8 s; take Δt ≈ 1 s for judging when A stops</text><text x="180.0" y="450.7" font-size="9" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">% uncertainty = 1/20.8 × 100%</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q3"><text x="411.7" y="498.7" font-size="10.5" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">5%</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q3"><text x="128.7" y="627.6" font-size="8.8" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">Better: the same ≈ 1 s judgement uncertainty is spread over twice the time, halving the</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q3"><text x="128.7" y="652.2" font-size="8.8" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">% uncertainty. Worse: the amplitudes have decayed, so B's stop is harder to see. Overall</text></g><g class="ans" data-q="Q3"><text x="128.7" y="676.6" font-size="8.8" text-anchor="start" fill="#1550c8">better, if B's stop is still clear.</text></g></svg>

notes.text: Keep both pendulums exactly 45 cm (top knot to bob centre); unequal lengths stop the energy transfer from being complete.
A never stops instantly. Its amplitude dwindles, so the uncertainty is a judgement of about ±1 s, not 0.01 s.
"Discuss": give both sides (smaller % uncertainty vs harder-to-see stop because of damping), then conclude.
